findings.problem: Most of the Big Idea walks through the verses in order instead of summing up what they mean. Line 1 covers Ephesians 2:1-3, line 3 covers Ephesians 2:4-7, line 4 covers Ephesians 2:8-9 and line 6 covers Ephesians 2:10, and each one mostly restates its verses clause by clause (for example line 3: "made us alive with Christ, raised us up and seated us with Him, so in the coming ages He could display..."). Only lines 2, 5 and 7 say what the passage means. The verse-by-verse lines should be reshaped into a summary of the meaning (dead people can't save themselves, God saves by grace as a gift, and good works follow as what we were made for) rather than a condensed run through the verses.

rule.text: A real summary of what the passage means, not a retelling of the verses.

findings.problem: Line 1 says "Paul says we were \"dead in your trespasses and sins,\"" and cites Ephesians 2:1-3. In Ephesians 2:1 the BSB says "And you were dead in your trespasses and sins,", so Paul is talking to the readers ("you"), not "we". The "we" wording comes later, in Ephesians 2:3 and 2:5 ("we were dead in our trespasses"). As written, the line makes Paul say "we" and then quotes him saying "your" in the same sentence. Either say "Paul tells them they were" before the Ephesians 2:1 quote, or quote Ephesians 2:5 ("dead in our trespasses") with the "we" wording.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
